summary: The study presents low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) of high-purity tin monosulfide (SnS) of both cubic and orthorhombic phases using tin(II) 2,4-pentanedionate [Sn(acac)2] and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) as precursors. The ALD process is self-limiting and stable over temperatures from at least 80 to 160 °C, with a stable mass gain of 19 ng cm−2 cycle−1. The SnS thin film crystal structure and morphology undergo significant changes depending on the conditions, with the cubic phase showing a direct forbidden-type bandgap of 1.64 eV and the orthorhombic phase displaying a wide Urbach tail in the near-infrared region.
